text: Hello and welcome to the live commentary of the Premier League clash between Chelsea and Aston Villa at Stamford Bridge.
Chelsea need to get back to winning ways in the Premier League after losing to Nottingham Forest and drawing with Bournemouth last time out.
Mauricio Pochettino's men have struggled in the final third, continuing their poor record in front of goal from the last campaign.
The Blues have only won one of their opening five games and are in dire need to a momentum boost to kickstart their season.
Villa have had an up and down start to the season.
Their campaign began with a 5-1 hammering against Newcastle United, but wins against Burnley, Everton and Crystal Palace have highlighted their prowess in front of goal.
However, there are defensive deficiencies that were on show against the Magpies, Liverpool and in their Europa Conference League defeat to Legia Warsaw last time out.
Unai Emery will be looking for an improvement from his side today.
Chelsea have made one change to their side that drew against Bournemouth last time out.
Caicedo returns from injury and replaces Ugochukwu in the middle of the park alongside Gallagher.
Pochettino keeps faith with the same backline that held the Cherries at bay as Colwill continues at left-back.
Chilwell remains on the bench.
Villa have made five changes to their side that was beaten by Legia Warsaw during the week.
Watkins is back to lead the line in place of Duran.
Diaby returns in place of Bailey in the final third, while Douglas Luiz joins Kamara in the midfield.
Torres and Cash are also restored to the back four.
The players are out on the pitch so we should be under way shortly.
We're under way at Stamford Bridge.
Mudryk releases the run of Fernandez over the top, but his cross back into the middle evades Jackson and the flag goes up late for offside anyway.
Mudryk almost pounces on a mistake from the visitors at the back, but Konsa gets across quickly to prevent him bearing down on goal.
SAVE! Douglas Luiz loses out to Fernandez and it allows Jackson to feed Caicedo.
The midfielder has space to fire at goal, but sends a tame effort straight at Martinez.
Sterling plays the give and go with Jackson down the right flank, but Torres gets across to force a corner.
Disasi tries to connect with Fernandez's corner from the right flank, but it skims his head.
It strikes Kamara on the arm, but the Chelsea appeals for a penalty are muted.
Chelsea are probing with menace down the right flank in the early stages through Sterling and Gusto, who are finding space in the wide areas.
Thiago Silva angles a ball over the top for Mudryk down the left flank.
He steers a cutback towards Jackson, but Konsa on the slide directs it away from danger.
Colwill makes a break down the left flank and he sends a low cross into the middle.
Kamara slides and he knocks the ball off Jackson's arm to earn Villa a free-kick.
Jackson makes a surge into the Chelsea half and skips past one challenge, but Kamara acts to win the ball back for the visitors using his frame to edge out the forward.
Digne gets forward and combines with Zaniolo, who wins a corner off the body of Gallagher.
WHAT A SAVE! Douglas Luiz whips a corner towards the near post that is deflected out to Digne.
He powers a strike towards goal on his left foot that Sanchez has to turn over the bar.
Jackson speeds into the box and has Sterling in support.
He goes down under pressure from Konsa, but the flag is up for offside anyway.
Fernandez is down after taking a knock in a challenge with Zaniolo.
He walks gingerly to his feet, which will something to monitor for Pochettino.
CHANCE! Mudryk threads the needle to release Jackson in the inside-left channel.
The forward goes for a first-time strike on his left foot, poking his effort towards goal, but Martinez diverts it behind.
Jackson had more time than he thought there.
Jackson has space in the final third, but he takes the path away from goal and his eventual cross towards Fernandez is nodded back to Martinez by Cash.
Chelsea are getting the ball in the right areas, but their decision-making with their final pass and shot has been their downfall today.
Cash is afforded space on the right flank and he takes on the early strike at goal that is deflected into the arms of Sanchez by Colwill.
The visitors have struggled to get control of possession, but have been alert in the final third.
With Villa's quality, the hosts cannot afford to lose the ball in their own half.
CHANCE! Gusto bursts down the right flank and cuts the ball back to Fernandez.
He has space and time, but scuffs his strike well wide of the target.
Fernandez had to hit the target there.
Watkins wins possession for the visitors following a loose pass from Colwill.
Caicedo brings down the forward on the charge 25 yards from goal, handing Villa a free-kick in a useful position.
Douglas Luiz lines up a strike at goal, but his effort clips the Chelsea wall and drifts wide for a corner.
SAVE! Sanchez rescues Chelsea again.
Kamara rises to head a corner from Douglas Luiz back into a dangerous area.
Zaniolo shoots on the turn on the volley, but sees his effort turned over the bar.
Digne latches onto another loose ball on the edge of the Chelsea box following a corner.
On this occasion, he lifts his effort comfortably over the top.
Mudryk surges past Cash down the left flank and places a perfect low ball across the face of goal, but both Jackson and Sterling are nowhere to be seen.
Jackson sends Gusto away down the right flank, but he is forced to wait for support and his cutback towards Gallagher is cleared behind.
DISALLOWED GOAL! Disasi heads Gusto's cross into the back of the net with a fine effort, but the offside flag cuts short his celebration.
Digne drags back Sterling on a run off the ball and goes into the book.
There will be three minutes of added time.
HALF-TIME: CHELSEA 0-0 ASTON VILLA
Despite signalling three minutes of added time, the half ends after only two.
It's goalless at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League clash between Chelsea and Aston Villa.
Villa have had the best chances of the game as Robert Sanchez has been called on twice to deny Lucas Digne and Nicolo Zaniolo with reaction stops.
At the other end, Chelsea have had the ball in the next, but Axel Disasi was offside, while Nicolas Jackson also missed a good opportunity.
It has been groundhog day for Chelsea in front of goal.
They've got themselves into good positions, but have lacked the clinical edge to get the breakthrough.
Disasi should have kept himself onside, while Jackson should have converted his opening.
Villa have looked dangerous at times, but have been exposed at the back as well.
We're back under way at Stamford Bridge.
SAVE! Thiago Silva releases Sterling over the top and through on goal.
He only has Martinez to beat as he bears down on the target, but the Villa keeper spreads himself to make the stop.
Fernandez curls a fine cross to the back post for Jackson to attack.
He connects with a header, but sends it just wide of the target.
The flag goes up for offside anyway.
Jackson is booked for encroachment.
OFFSIDE! Chelsea are in behind the high Aston Villa line again.
Sterling bursts through on goal, but sees his effort blocked.
Once again, the flag goes up late.
Sterling and Jackson need to start timing these runs.
Martinez takes a loose touch before his clearance downfield and it results in Jackson blocking the ball, but it bounces back for a goal-kick.
Gusto could be in trouble here as he catches Digne on the ankle with his boot.
The referee is being told to look at the screen at the side of the field.
OFF! Gusto is sent off.
Having initially been given a yellow card, Gusto's punishment is upgraded to a red for catching Digne on the ankle with an outstretched boot after a VAR check.
Chelsea are down to 10 men.
SCRAMBLE! Cash and Douglas Luiz force efforts at goal around the Chelsea box, but the wall of blue shirts hold firm in front of the net to concede only a corner.
Mudryk makes way for Chilwell to shore up the Chelsea defence following Gusto's dismissal.
Zaniolo collects in the final third and has space to shoot, but he sees his effort charged down by Thiago Silva.
Cash goes for a blast from distance, but Sanchez watches it carefully into his hands.
Villa are upping the ante now.
Caicedo sends an early ball over the top for Jackson, but he takes a poor first touch and allows Konsa to recover to edge him out in the Villa box.
Gusto, aged 20 years and 128 days, is the third-youngest Chelsea player to receive a Premier League red card.
Ugochukwu enters the action to replace Jackson to shore up the Chelsea midfield.
Palmer is on for Fernandez in the final third.
DIABY HAS TO HIT THE TARGET! The winger collects the ball following a loose header at the back post.
He shoots first time, but scuffs his effort into the ground and wide of the target.
GOALLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL!!!!!! WATKINS SCORES ON THE BREAK!!!!! 1-0 VILLA! Chelsea pay the price for committing too many men forward as Watkins produces a clinical finish.
Gallagher's cutback evades every blue shirt in the box and Villa work the ball forward.
Diaby feeds Watkins, who faces off against Colwill on his run into the box.
Colwill blocks his first shot, but he buries the second with a finish off the inside of the left post.
Ramsey enters the action to replace McGinn in the Villa midfield.
Bailey replaces Zaniolo in the final third.
SAVE! Chilwell is played into space and only has Martinez to beat, but he fires his left-footed strike straight at Martinez.
Palmer times his throughball to perfection to release Disasi down the right flank.
He opens up space to strike at goal on his right foot, but slices his effort wide of the target.
Caicedo is withdrawn as Chelsea need goals.
Broja replaces the midfielder.
Watkins sends Diaby through on goal and he surges into the box.
He fires low and hard, but Sanchez makes a sharp stop.
The flag may have gone up on review there.
Tielemans enters the action for Villa in their midfield for Diaby.
SAVE! Sanchez keeps Chelsea in the game as he turns a curling strike from Ramsey past the post that was seemingly destined for the bottom-right corner.
Konsa attacks the resulting corner from Bailey, only to plant his header over the top.
Chelsea win a free-kick on the left flank that Chilwell delivers deep to the back post that Broja fails to connect with on the slide.
Chilwell brings down Watkins on the charge and goes into the book.
Dendoncker comes on to replace the impressive Kamara.
There will be 11 minutes of added time.
Duran replaces Watkins for the closing stages of the contest.
Douglas Luiz brings down Sterling and is booked.
BLOCK! Konsa sticks out a boot at the vital moment to prevent Palmer's low strike from finding the net after great work from Disasi down the right flank.
Martinez is booked for timewasting.
Sanchez has a concerning moment as a he drops a corner from Douglas Luiz from the left flank, but there was no one in a Villa shirt there to capitalise.
Time is running out for Chelsea to earn a share of the spoils.
The Blues have not been good enough in the final third.
Gallagher tees up Palmer for a drive on the edge of the box.
He drills a left-footed strike at goal, which is charged down by two defenders.
Bailey pulls back Chilwell on the left flank.
Chelsea will have one final chance to send cross into the box.
OFFSIDE! Chelsea see the offside flag raised again as Broja heads Chilwell's cross wide.
It has been the story of their day.
Chelsea have been caught offside on 10 occasions today.
FULL-TIME: CHELSEA 0-1 ASTON VILLA
Aston Villa inflict further pain on Chelsea with a 1-0 win in their Premier League clash at Stamford Bridge.
After a goalless first period, Malo Gusto was sent off after a VAR checked overturned his yellow card and awarded a red card for a challenge on Lucas Digne in the second half.
Villa upped the ante with their numerical advantage and took the lead through a counter as Ollie Watkins buried his chance on the break.

The Blues' problems in goal persisted as they failed to find the back of the net for the third game on the bounce and have now only taken one point out of a possible nine from their last three matches.
Villa move up to sixth with their victory.
Chelsea are next in action in the EFL Cup against Brighton next week at home.
Villa take on Everton in their EFL Cup game on Wednesday at Villa Park.
Thanks for joining our commentary today.
Until next time, goodbye.
